standard_prerequisites.name: Counting square-full integers
standard_prerequisites.statement: There are O(sqrt z) square-full integers at most z; each can be written a^2b^3 with b square-free, and sum_b b^(-3/2) converges.
standard_prerequisites.use: Bound the square-full allocation count and the moment sum. No boundary probability estimate is supplied.

core_obligations: Use multiplicativity to remove arbitrary allocations of the square-full part while retaining a controlled window for the square-free divisor.
Translate the k-coordinate allocation weights exactly to alpha^omega(d)*(1-alpha)^omega(m) on the square-free part.
Track the dyadic square-free scale and split the factor pair at sqrt(2x/z), maintaining uniform control near u=0 and u=1.
Sum the scale loss(log z)/sqrt z after excluding the small square-free part using a fractional moment.

proof_roadmap.step: A square-full divisor moment makes N-flat<=x/(log x)^3 negligible; then decompose the remaining event by dyadic x/N-flat.
Separate square-free and square-full prime powers, sum out the latter allocations, and reduce to a weighted divisor pair with product of order x/z.
Use two asymmetric hyperbola regions and the weighted mean/harmonic bounds to recover both endpoint factors uniformly.
Provide the author Euler-product/partial-summation proof for the harmonic-window tool rather than assuming that local estimate for free.

difficulty_reason: The input mean-value bound does not locate the factorization near x^u or control the random square-free deficit. The proof must decouple arbitrary multiplicative allocation weights on the square-full part, identify the exact two complementary square-free weights, and choose a dyadic/hyperbola split that retains the distinct u and1-u endpoint exponents uniformly in alpha and the allocation rule f. This is a nonroutine analytic-number-theoretic probability estimate, proposed as H2 for independent review.

compared.difference: Old prime/PD expected logarithmic discrepancy coupling does not supply the arithmetic divisor-window boundary estimate.

The correlated PD Dirichlet estimate uses two-point Mecke and beta windows; this integer-factorization bound uses squarefull/flat coprime decomposition and hyperbola sums. They bound different random objects and require independent arguments; the final combined Dirichlet law is not counted as a third consequence.
